newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision to use proceeds to pay debt.
newsitem.headline: Cablevision to use proceeds to pay debt.

text.p: Cablevision Systems Corp will use its proceeds from Rainbow Media Holdings Inc's deal with Fox/Liberty Networks to reduce debt, Cablevision Vice Chairman Marc Lustgarten said Monday.
Lustgarten told reporters the proceeds will pay down $1.25 billion in debt that Rainbow has assumed from buying the Madison Square Garden sports business in New York.
"Most of the proceeds is going to be used to pay down debt," Lustgarten said.
Fox/Liberty has agreed to invest $850 million for a 40 percent stake in Rainbow's sports interests.
Lustgarten shied away from projecting how much in revenues the new Fox/Liberty-Rainbow ventures would generate for Cablevision, which owns 75 percent of Rainbow.
"Only time will tell," he said. But he said the new venture "should create a great deal more cash flow."
Lustgarten said the deal was an alternative for national advertisers on the ESPN all-sports U.S. channels who want to buy commercial time on local sports broadcasts.
"Fox/Liberty had one-half of an (advertising) dollar bill, and we had one half," Lustgarten said. "Now we're uniting, and that one dollar turns into 10 dollars."

Under the deal, Rainbow will be managing partner in the jointly owned sports venture. The various sports networks that go into the entity will be 60 percent owned by Rainbow and 40 percent by Fox/Liberty.

In April, Cablevision signed a definitive deal to buy out ITT Corp's 50 percent partnership in MSG, which includes basketball and hockey teams and the MSG televison network. The companies teamed up in 1995 to buy the Garden for $1 billion.
Fox/Liberty is a joint venture of News Corp's Fox Sports unit and Liberty Media Corp, a unit of Tele-Communications Inc.
Rainbow is 25 percent owned by General Electric Co's NBC unit.
